 Dylan Rourke has been cast as Jason Duval, one of the two central characters in Rockstar Games ' Grand Theft Auto 6 . The actor joins Manni L. Perez, who portrays Lucia, in the crime-focused video game set in modern-day Vice City, where the protagonists attempt to survive and succeed in a dangerous criminal underworld.
 Jason and Lucia form the game's two-character playable lineup, marking another change in the franchise's approach to its main protagonists. Rourke's involvement brings an actor with experience in television, theater, improvisational comedy, and sketch performance to the highly anticipated production. According to information reported by SVG, Rourke's acting career dates back to 2013.

 His television appearances include three episodes of Station 19, in which he played emergency medical technician Todd.

 He also appeared in an episode of Grey's Anatomy, the medical drama connected to Station 19. His other television credits include Shooter and 911: Lone Star.
 Rourke has also built experience on the stage. He portrayed Happy Loman in a California production of Death of a Salesman, appearing alongside Rob Morrow and Robert Adamson. The character has a notable theatrical history. Previous Broadway performers in the role include Harvey Keitel, Finn Wittrock, and Stephen Lang.
 His comedy background includes performances with The Groundlings, Upright Citizens Brigade, and Second City. These organizations are established names in the American improvisational and sketch comedy scene. Rourke also performed alongside veteran comedian Fred Willard as part of The MoHo Group in Los Angeles. His experience across different entertainment formats adds to his professional background ahead of the game's release.
 Also Read 
 Rockstar Details More Than 1000 GTA 6 World Encounters 
 Jason's character represents one half of a story that combines criminal drama with satirical portrayals of American culture. The Grand Theft Auto franchise has traditionally blended serious crime narratives with irreverent humor and social commentary. Previous installments adopted different approaches to their central characters.
 In 2008, Michael Hollick portrayed Niko Bellic in Grand Theft Auto IV, while downloadable expansions introduced Johnny and Luis, played by Scott Hill and Mario D'Leon, respectively. Grand Theft Auto V followed in 2013 with three playable protagonists: Michael, Franklin, and Trevor. Their performances were provided by Ned Luke, Shawn Fonteno, and Steven Ogg, respectively.
 The series' tonal direction has also generated debate among players. Some fans considered Grand Theft Auto IV excessively serious, while others expressed the opposite criticism of Grand Theft Auto V.

 Rockstar Games subsequently received praise for its storytelling approach in 2018's Red Dead Redemption II. Early reviews of Grand Theft Auto 6 have described the upcoming installment as a major achievement that builds on that narrative foundation. Meanwhile, Manni L.
 Perez's portrayal of Lucia has attracted attention through a nomination at The Game Awards, organized by Geoff Keighley. Her recognition has also increased interest in the partnership between the game's two central characters.
